title: Pin the guard job's env wiring, and make the suite print its own interpreter
description: Two peer findings. lore-cli (PR #119): deleting the workflow fetch line survived its suite at 0 red until a WIRING assertion pinned it - the script-level test exercises the diagnosis, a different site from the wiring. Applied here: our wiring test pins the run: line and fetch-depth: 0 but NOT the env block. Measured, not reasoned: BEFORE_SHA miswired to github.sha exits 0 GREEN with main unchanged at <sha> - a permanently always-green gate; deleting the env block exits 1 loudly. Only the silent one matters and nothing catches it. opum-doc (ODOC-216): fixed our shared bash-version claim FORWARD by having the suite print environment: bash VERSION, git VERSION above its verdict - cheaper than making the CI job print it, and it covers local runs where the same claim gets made.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The wiring test pins BEFORE_SHA to github.event.before and FORCED to github.event.forced; miswiring either in the workflow turns the suite red
The suite prints its own bash and git versions above the verdict, so local and CI runs each name their interpreter instead of a reader trusting a written claim
All five existing mutants still die after the change, re-run AFTER the fix per OMARK-59, plus the two new env mutants

comments.body: SUPERSEDED, in this record only. This final summary says "Still unproven: that GitHub populates BEFORE_SHA correctly at runtime; this pins the workflow TEXT only, and the runtime half waits on this repos first real promotion." That promotion has since happened - run 35031089133 on 65c3be9 - and the guard printed "main moved forward 432b959... -> 65c3be97...", where 432b959 matches the promotion pushs own 432b959..65c3be9 output. So BEFORE_SHA does arrive from github.event.before with mains true previous HEAD. OMARK-61 records it in the test file; this comment records it here, because the fix that corrected the file left this record saying the opposite. Bounded: FORCED was false throughout, the all-zeros path never ran, and no FAILING branch has run against real Actions inputs. Found by applying quest-clis enumeration rule (routed via opum-doc ODOC-216): when a fix corrects a claim, enumerate every place the claim is made. The other site was PR #120s body, corrected by comment there.

finalSummary: Delivered in PR #121, CI run 35030273898. The suite now prints its environment and CI's own log reads 'environment: bash 5.2.21(1)-release, git version 2.55.0' with 'passed 19, failed 0' - so the bash version OMARK-59 asserted from the runner image's reputation is now MEASURED rather than claimed, and happened to be right, which is exactly why it was worth measuring. Wiring test pins BEFORE_SHA to github.event.before and FORCED to github.event.forced. Mutation run, each predicted and re-run AFTER the change: script assertion 1 -> DIED 5 red, 2 -> DIED 1, 3 -> DIED 3, drop refspec -> DIED 1, restore 2>/dev/null -> DIED 1; workflow BEFORE_SHA -> github.sha -> DIED 1, env block deleted -> DIED 2. The load-bearing measurement: miswiring BEFORE_SHA exits 0 GREEN ('main unchanged at <sha>') while deleting the env block exits 1 loudly - only the silent one could survive unnoticed, and no script can detect it from inside. Still unproven: that GitHub populates BEFORE_SHA correctly at runtime; this pins the workflow TEXT only, and the runtime half waits on this repo's first real promotion.
